appSubtitle: Learn how electric coils shape magnetic fields

injection.title: Particle Injection
injection.hint: Navigate with WASD + arrow keys. Arrow keys look around; WASD moves. Press Space to inject a particle.

home.title: Welcome to Magnetic Field Explorer
home.subtitle: Choose a lesson below to explore how electric currents shape magnetic fields.

cards.singleLoop: The Biot-Savart field of a single circular loop — the building block of every coil geometry. Field lines form closed dipole loops; on-axis strength is plotted in real time.
cards.helmholtz: Two coaxial loops in Helmholtz configuration produce a highly uniform field between them. Flip one current to switch to the anti-Helmholtz (magnetic mirror) arrangement.
cards.toroidal: N coils arranged around a torus create a toroidal field (B ∝ 1/R). Curvature and gradient drifts prevent confinement by a toroidal field alone — the motivation for adding a poloidal component.
cards.tokamak: Toroidal coils plus a plasma current Iₚ generate a poloidal field that twists the field lines into helices. Adjust the ITER preset to explore reactor-scale geometry and keV particle orbits.
cards.gradient: A model field Bz(x) = B₀ + α·x² + β·x⁴ along z. The transverse gradient drives injected particles to precess in y — illustrating gradient drift without solving the full Maxwell equations.
cards.stellarator: 50 non-planar coils extracted from the W7-X CAD model, each discretized into 63 Biot–Savart segments. Field lines are traced through the vacuum magnetic field computed from the full coil set.

fieldReview.title: Field-review mode
fieldReview.desc: The default mode. Inspect field lines and coil geometry by orbiting around the scene with your mouse.

injection.title: Particle-injection mode
injection.desc: Activated via the "Enable" button in the Injection panel. Fly through the field in first-person and fire particles.
injection.space: Inject a particle in the current view direction

descriptions.singleLoop: A single circular current loop produces a dipole-like magnetic field. Field lines form closed loops threading through the coil. On axis: Bz = μ₀Ia²/[2(a²+z²)^(3/2)], peaking at the centre and falling as z⁻³ far away.
descriptions.helmholtz: Two coaxial coils of radius R separated by distance R (the Helmholtz condition) produce a remarkably uniform field in the region between them. Widely used in laboratories to cancel the Earth's magnetic field or provide a controlled background.
descriptions.antiHelmholtz: Reversing one coil current creates a magnetic mirror: the field vanishes at the midplane and strengthens near each coil. The resulting ∇B reflects charged particles back from both ends — the basic trapping mechanism in mirror-machine fusion concepts.
descriptions.toroidal: N coils arranged symmetrically around a torus produce a toroidal field with B ∝ 1/R (strongest at the inner edge). Curvature and gradient drifts cause particles to drift vertically and escape — the reason a pure toroidal field cannot confine a plasma, and the motivation for adding a poloidal component in a tokamak.
descriptions.tokamak: A plasma current Iₚ flowing toroidally induces a poloidal field around the minor cross-section (Ampère: Bθ ≈ μ₀Iₚ/2πr). Combined with the toroidal coil field, this twists field lines into helices that close on themselves, providing confinement. The rotational transform ι = Bθ R₀/(Bφ r) sets how many poloidal turns a field line makes per toroidal circuit.
descriptions.gradient: A model field Bz(x) = B₀ + α·x² + β·x⁴ pointing purely along z — even in x, so x = 0 is always a field extremum. Because Bx = By = 0 everywhere, ∇×B ≠ 0 and this is not a physical vacuum field. It is a pedagogical tool: the transverse ∇Bz drives gradient drift, causing injected particles to precess in the y-direction.
descriptions.stellarator: A scaled W7-X stellarator with 50 non-planar coils extracted from the CAD geometry. The magnetic field is computed via the Biot–Savart law over 3150 coil segments, producing a vacuum field with nested flux surfaces and rotational transform. Use field-line tracing and particle injection to explore confinement in a realistic 3D coil topology.
descriptions.helicalSheet: A radial line of starting points is advected along field lines. The rotational transform ι(r) ∝ r causes outer lines to wind faster, shearing the initial straight line into a helical sheet.
